title: adaptive-runway-grid-hiring-swaps-and-price-corridor-prototype
content:
Summary:
This sandbox models an adaptive runway grid that couples discretionary hiring swaps (role reallocation, contractor-for-hire exchange) with a dynamic pricing corridor. Goal: quantify how small price moves or a staged hiring-swap program extend runway under token-demand surges and regression in revenue conversion.

Key baseline inputs (current runbook):
- Cash runway (uncommitted): $42.4M
- Monthly burn (base, before actions): $3.1M
- Current headcount baseline (full-time equivalents): 152 total (eng 78, infra 18, product 14, sales/growth 20, go-to-market ops 10, finance/support 12)
- Average loaded cost per FTE (all-in): $17.5k/mo
- Committed Dedicated contracts / reserves: estimated $1.05M/mo (GPU / infra reserved)
- Typical revenue sensitivity window: 3 months lag to pricing changes

Assumptions for scenarios:
1) Hiring-swap program: discretionary swaps allow converting 8 mid/senior eng FTEs to contractor-led pods or delaying 6 hires for 6 months. Net immediate cash delta: -$0.15M/mo (savings), with a 12% productivity drag (measured risk).
2) Price corridor: temporary token surcharge / discount band of +/-10% applied to new enterprise commitments (affects conversion and churn; see elasticity). Lead effect on realized revenue assumes 30% of ARR is responsive within 60d.
3) Spot GPU costs oscillate ±18% across regions; plan uses conservative +10% headroom.

Scenario matrix (simplified):
Columns: Action / Price delta / Net monthly burn / Runway months (approx)
- Baseline / 0% / $3.10M / 13.7 months
- Hiring-swap only / 0% / $2.95M / 14.4 months
- Price +8% corridor, conservative take / +8% / $2.95M net (with revenue lift) / 17.2 months
- Price -6% to stimulate volume / -6% / $3.05M net (short-term revenue dip) / 14.0 months
- Combined swap + price +8% / +8% / $2.80M net / 18.9 months
- Aggressive freeze (all discretionary hires frozen) / 0% / $2.60M / 20.5 months

Quick sensitivity grid (price delta vs runway impact):
- -15% price -> runway drops by ~2.2 months (volume not enough to offset unit decline)
- -5% price -> runway neutral to -0.4 months depending on conversion
- +5% price -> runway +1.1 months (if conversion hold)
- +10% price -> runway +2.8 months (higher uplift observed in pilot cohorts)

Headcount reallocation template (monthly cash impact):
- Swap 1 mid-sr Eng -> contractor pod: saves $12k/mo each net (after contractor premium), productivity risk +10%
- Delay 1 senior hire (offer accepted, start delayed 3 months): saves $22k/mo for delay period
- Redeploy 2 growth reps from lower-ROI deals to onboarding success (nil cash change, positive downstream ARR retention)

Risk-adjusted KPIs to track if we run prototype: 
- Realized conversion delta (cohort A/B) at +8% price (target >+9% net ARR lift per cohort)
- Customer churn 90d after corridor changes (must be <1.1x baseline)
- Eng throughput (PRs merged / sprint velocity) under swap program (-12% threshold triggers rollback)
- Cost-to-serve per route (tokens-per-dollar) by model family

Operational playbook (stretch):
Week 0: Exec approval of corridor bounds (+/- up to 10%) and opt-in enterprise segments.
Week 1-2: Launch hiring-swap pilot in one eng squad (3 FTEs swapped to contractor pods). Measure weekly velocity and bug rate.
Week 3-8: Stagger price corridor to 20% of new signups; monitor conversion lag. Run parallel A/B.
Week 9: Evaluate net cashflow delta and decide scale to company-wide or roll back.

Edge cases and notes to reviewers (open items):
- Legal: need review on contract amendment language for temporary corridor and on pro-ration mechanics.
- Sales comp: adjust quota/commission for accounts sold during corridor window (impact to OPEX).
- Accounting: recognize revenue timing differences if price changes mid-contract quarter.
- Product: quality guardrails for swap-induced productivity dips (automated regression tests ramp).

Small tables (estimates) - monthly P&L delta examples (rounded):
- Baseline: revenue $1.8M, gross op costs $0.9M, infra & GPUs $0.45M, payroll $0.75M -> net burn $3.1M (after credits/prefunds)
- With +8% price (pilot capture): revenue $1.94M (+$144k), costs unchanged -> net burn ~ $2.96M (improves runway ~2.8 months)
- With hiring-swap (pilot): payroll 0.75 -> 0.68M (saves $70k), but contractor premium & overhead adds back $10k -> net saving $60k/mo

Open questions for finance/legal review panel:
- What guardrail for permanent churn would trigger immediate rollback of corridor? Proposed: >1.3x baseline churn over 60d.
- Approve nexus for commission true-ups? (Sales ops input required)
- Is a staged price corridor limited to 3 quarters maximum without board notice?

Appendix (experimental metrics):
- Elasticities used (pilot cohort): price elasticity = -0.34 (enterprise), -0.85 (startup segment)
- Productivity drag assumed per swap = 0.12 (12%); confidence: medium-low
- GPU cost headroom applied = +10% conservative margin

Notes to self (fragments / TODO):
- Build small dashboard: cohort conversion / churn / net cash delta by week.
- Wire in model to token mix per route (embed vs gen) to better allocate price deltas.
- Run headcount-swap labor model against SRE & infra critical-path roles separately (differing risk profiles).

End of sheet.
